observation_summary: The compiler crashes with a StackOverflowError when processing deeply nested binary operator expressions (e.g., many additions).
hypothesis: The recursive implementation of binary operator generation in CodeGenerator.add() causes stack exhaustion for deep expression trees. The fix replaces this recursion with an iterative 'unrollBinaryOperator' method to handle deep trees without consuming stack frames.
prediction: The code will show a transition from a recursive call structure (add -> addExpr -> add) to an iterative loop structure that processes the operator list without deep recursion.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace shows deep recursion between add() and addExpr(). The fix diff confirms the replacement of the recursive logic with a call to 'unrollBinaryOperator', which implements an iterative 'do-while' loop to traverse the expression tree, thus preventing stack overflow.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic stack overflow caused by an inefficient recursive algorithm for processing deep expression trees. The fix involves rewriting the procedural logic from a recursive approach to an iterative one (unrolling the binary operator), which is a quintessential 'Algorithm/Method' correction.
evidence_used: Stack trace showing deep recursion between CodeGenerator.add and CodeGenerator.addExpr
Fix diff showing replacement of recursive calls with unrollBinaryOperator
Fix diff showing the implementation of unrollBinaryOperator using a do-while loop
